role: XCUITest that Settings → Appearance is reachable, shows Light/Dim/Dark theme controls, and that tapping Dark does not kill the app.

flags.text: Passes the bare '-UITests' launch argument, which no production code reads (only -UITests-FreshInstall at AppLaunchRecovery.swift:185 and -UITests-ForcePaywall/-UITests-SeedArchive at UITestLaunchArguments.swift:18,23 are checked); it is inert

units.does: Sets continueAfterFailure=false, creates XCUIApplication, appends launch arguments -UITests, -UITests-FreshInstall and English locale (UITestLanguage.english), launches the app (the app wipes onboarding/disclaimer/paywall flags, settings files and the session archive via AppLaunchRecovery.resetUITestStateIfRequested) and walks every first-run gate with UITestLaunch.toMainUI, ignoring its Bool result.
units.entry: XCTest runner: setUp before each test in the class

units.does: Releases the XCUIApplication (app = nil); does not terminate the app.
units.entry: XCTest runner: tearDown after each test in the class

units.does: Asserts Settings opens via More, scrolls to settings.appearance, asserts it exists and taps it.

branches.effect: return without tapping (assertion above already failed)

units.does: Opens Appearance and asserts any static text or button containing 'Light', 'Dim' or 'Dark' exists.
units.entry: XCTest runner: test method on an XCTestCase subclass

flags.text: Passes if any one of three common substrings appears anywhere on screen, so it does not verify a theme picker exists (doc claims all three options are exposed)

units.does: Opens Appearance, skips if no 'Dark' button appears, taps it via tapSafely (result ignored) and asserts the tab bar still exists.
units.entry: XCTest runner: test method on an XCTestCase subclass

flags.text: Ignores tapSafely's result and asserts only that the tab bar exists (it stays in the hierarchy on any screen), so the theme switch may never have happened; XCTSkipUnless turns a missing button into a skip
